question: What main health problem happens when pregnancies are spaced too close together?

options.A: Elevated risk of adult-onset diabetes mellitus
options.B: Permanent loss of primary visual acuity
options.C: Premature fusion of cranial sutures in infants

explanation: Pregnancies that happen too close together do not give the mother's body enough time to rebuild her nutrient stores, which frequently leads to severe anemia. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why does leaving enough time between pregnancies protect the uterus?

options.A: It gives the uterine muscle and lining time to regain complete structural integrity
options.B: It permanently thickens the outer peritoneal layer of the pelvic cavity
options.C: It lowers overall systemic blood pressure in the pelvic blood vessels
options.D: It prevents the ovaries from releasing eggs during lactation

explanation: Giving the reproductive organs time to heal ensures the uterine tissue is strong enough to handle the demands of another pregnancy and labor. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h1)

question: When can a mother who is NOT breastfeeding start releasing eggs again after childbirth?

options.A: Exactly six months after placental delivery
options.B: As early as four to six weeks postpartum
options.C: Only after complete involution of the uterus
options.D: Only after three consecutive menstrual cycles

explanation: Without breastfeeding to suppress hormones, the monthly cycle often restarts within a month or two after birth, well before most women expect it. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why is it risky to wait for your first monthly period to return before using contraception?

options.A: Ovulation consistently happens before the first period returns
options.B: The first period is always too light to indicate fertility
options.C: Menstrual blood quality changes significantly after childbirth
options.D: Hormonal contraceptives prevent the return of menstruation permanently

explanation: An egg is released before the bleeding starts, meaning a woman can become pregnant before she even realizes her fertility has returned. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h2)

question: When is the best time for midwives to start talking about family planning with pregnant women?

options.A: Immediately after the placenta is delivered
options.B: When the child is weaned from the breast
options.C: Only at the six-week postnatal check

explanation: Bringing up family planning early during antenatal visits gives couples plenty of time to discuss and choose their postpartum options before the baby arrives. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h3)

question: A new mother is worried that a certain contraceptive will cause heavy bleeding and make her husband unhappy. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Delay all contraception counseling until her husband can attend the clinic
options.B: Tell her that cultural beliefs about bleeding are completely outdated
options.C: Listen actively to her concerns and discuss side effect management options
options.D: Insist that she choose an intrauterine device because it has no hormones

explanation: Listening to a client's personal and marital worries builds trust and helps her find a method she feels comfortable using. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the strict rules required for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) to work?

options.A: The infant must sleep through the night without feeding
options.B: The mother must remain completely without postpartum menses
options.C: The infant must nurse frequently throughout day and night
options.D: The baby must be exclusively or nearly exclusively breastfed

explanation: Long gaps in feeding at night cause prolactin hormones to drop, which allows fertility to return and breaks the rules of LAM. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why does giving an infant regular solid foods lower the birth control effectiveness of breastfeeding?

options.A: It directly stimulates the mother's ovaries to release an egg
options.B: It decreases the frequency and intensity of suckling at the breast
options.C: It neutralizes the hormonal feedback loop in the infant's digestive tract
options.D: It permanently stops the production of breastmilk within forty-eight hours

explanation: When a baby fills up on other foods, they breastfeed less often, which changes the mother's hormone levels and can bring back ovulation. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why are combined estrogen-progestogen birth control methods generally avoided during the first three weeks after birth?

options.A: They increase the risk of blood clots and can reduce milk supply
options.B: They accelerate the natural involution of the uterine muscle
options.C: They cause immediate permanent cessation of lochia flow
options.D: They make the infant hypersensitive to synthetic hormones

explanation: Postpartum women already have a higher chance of developing blood clots, and estrogen adds to this risk while also slowing down milk production. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h5)

question: A breastfeeding mother who gave birth two weeks ago wants a safe hormonal contraceptive that won't hurt her milk supply. What is the best choice?
explanation: Progestogen-only methods do not interfere with breastmilk production and are completely safe to use during the early weeks after delivery. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the main drawback of putting in an intrauterine device (IUD) right after childbirth compared to waiting later?

options.A: A complete suppression of lochial drainage
options.B: Permanent scarring of the internal cervical os
options.C: A higher rate of spontaneous device expulsion
options.D: An increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Because the uterus and cervix are still large and relaxed right after birth, the body is more likely to push the device out on its own. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h6)

question: What happens to a woman's ability to have children right after an IUD is removed?

options.A: She remains temporarily sterile for one year
options.B: It takes at least six months for eggs to mature
options.C: Fertility returns right away with no delay
options.D: Her ovulation cycle is permanently suppressed

explanation: IUDs work locally and do not use hormones to block ovulation, meaning normal fertility comes back instantly when the device is taken out. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is a common myth about modern family planning methods in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: They make breastmilk turn sweet and spoil quickly
options.B: They instantly cure all forms of postpartum depression
options.C: They cause permanent sterility or accumulate inside the stomach
options.D: They guarantee that every future baby will be a male child

explanation: A widespread misunderstanding is that modern contraceptives stay trapped inside the body or permanently ruin a woman's ability to get pregnant. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h7)

question: A patient wants an implant but is scared because her mother-in-law says contraceptives rot inside the womb. How should the midwife reply?

options.A: Tell the client to ignore her mother-in-law completely and get the implant in secret
options.B: Refuse to provide any family planning until the entire extended family attends clinic
options.C: Agree with the mother-in-law's warning and suggest traditional herbs instead
options.D: Provide clear, respectful education that debunks the myth and offer to speak with the family if desired

explanation: Respectful conversation bridges the gap between traditional fears and medical facts without disrespecting the patient's family support system. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h7)
